grh_324f656c018e383abadf.title: A Bad Case Of Quarantine
paragraphs: Nine-year-old Patsy Robinson is recovering from measles just as her older brother Bud is preparing for a school dance with Merrily Hamlin. Bud soon comes down with the measles himself and must stay home, so visiting cousin Lester takes Merrily to the dance in his place. Lester proves such a good dancer that Merrily begins spending more time with him even after Bud recovers, leaving Bud jealous and convinced that the college-age cousin has stolen his girl. Patsy, feeling guilty for having given Bud the measles, quietly takes matters into her own hands when she realizes she is coming down with mumps. She carefully keeps everyone away except Lester, making sure he is the one exposed. Lester is quarantined until just before he is due to leave town, while Bud is sent to stay safely with the Hamlins. With Lester out of competition, Merrily makes clear that she really prefers Bud and plans to attend the basketball dance with him. Christian recognizes exactly what Patsy has done and rewards her protective little-sister plotting with an ice-cream soda.

grh_32df5a49f73b1d7c4257.title: Juliet Said It
paragraphs: Carol Tucker works as a nurse's aide while her husband, Sergeant Mark Tucker, serves overseas and her injured young brother-in-law Skip recovers in the hospital. Lonely and uncertain about Mark, Carol becomes fascinated by a glamorous visitor who presents himself as an RAF wing commander and former Russian prince. His stories and decorations impress the town, and after Mark is reported missing in action Carol begins to believe she may be falling in love with the supposed hero. Dr. Christian grows suspicious, especially after the man avoids a medical examination following an automobile accident. Skip's scrapbook of military decorations gives Christian the clue: the commander's claimed medal and the date he says he received it do not fit the actual history. Confronted, the impostor cannot produce proper papers and is taken by military police. Almost immediately a new War Department message reports that Mark is alive in a German prisoner-of-war camp and has been awarded the Silver Star for gallantry. Christian replaces the false hero at the town rally with the story of the real one, while Carol recognizes where her loyalty and love truly belong.

grh_32bf2159165101ab5d05.title: The Guileless Gypsy
paragraphs: While seeking information from a Romany camp, Holmes is drawn into threats against a wealthy family's young heir that appear to come from the gypsies. The wording of a kidnapping note betrays the fraud because a true Romany would not have used the term written in the threat. Holmes secretly places the boy with Jasper Hearn's people for protection, but Major Treadgold lays a dawn trap for Holmes at the Braxton Quagmire. Lydia, a gypsy violinist, reads the warning and goes in Holmes's coat and deerstalker instead; Treadgold shoots her, and with her dying words she identifies him. The tribe drives Treadgold into the quagmire, ending his scheme to frame and expel them, and Lydia leaves Holmes her violin.

grh_329138d71c660ce45009.title: Hildy
paragraphs: Illustrator Edward Gaskin and his wife Joan adopt a dog named Hildy shortly before their elderly dog Sam dies. One snowy morning Edward runs for a train and crashes into a steel girder, suffering a severe head injury that leaves his right side paralyzed and initially robs him of speech. Back home he grows bitter, resents Joan for working, rejects friends and even contemplates suicide because he believes his life and career are finished. Joan finally confronts his self-pity, and Edward begins trying to rebuild his life, drawing with his left hand and accepting help. Hildy repeatedly places a ball in Edward's useless right hand and nudges the arm through the same motion. One day he unexpectedly holds and throws the ball, and soon he can lift a fork with that hand. Edward credits Hildy's persistence with helping give him his life back.

grh_32c341367ce9b5a5efb8.title: Man To Man
paragraphs: Young Nicky Marshall, grieving the recent death of his father, asks Dr. Christian to marry his widowed mother because he longs for a little brother or sister and believes a new father is the only way that can happen. Dr. Christian gently explains that no one can replace the father Nicky's mother still loves, then widens the boy's idea of family by showing him how children of different backgrounds can live as brothers and sisters in one world. The conversation becomes unexpectedly personal when Nicky's mother telephones with news Dr. Christian has not yet known: she is already expecting another child by her late husband. Nicky leaves overjoyed that he will have the brother or sister he wanted without replacing the father he still loves.

paragraphs: Scientists at Stellar Observatory receive an extraordinarily powerful repeating radio signal and initially believe an intelligent civilization, or even some higher intelligence, may be trying to contact Earth. The public and press wait while researchers decode the transmission. Its frequency eventually reveals that the source is not alien at all but one of humanity's own lost satellites, swept into a distant solar orbit and re-energized by powerful planetary magnetic fields.
